meta.title: Konechi — see whether you are on ethernet or Wi-Fi
meta.description: A tiny macOS menu bar app that shows, at a glance, whether your Mac is connected by cable or over Wi-Fi.

hero.tagline: Cable or Wi-Fi, at a glance
hero.lead: macOS only tells you about Wi-Fi. Konechi sits in your menu bar and shows which link is actually carrying your traffic.

states.title: She reacts to your connection
states.lead: On top form when the cable is in, doing fine on Wi-Fi, out of energy when nothing is connected.

truth.title: The link actually in use
truth.body: It reads the primary interface of the default route from the system itself, rather than guessing. Plug in a cable while Wi-Fi is still on and it switches immediately.

details.title: The details, one click away
details.body: Service name, device, IP address, router and link speed. Throughput is measured every second, but only while the menu is open.

vpn.title: VPN, without losing the link
vpn.body: When your traffic runs through a tunnel, a padlock appears over the physical link underneath — so you still know whether you are on cable or Wi-Fi.

quiet.title: Out of the way
quiet.body: No dock icon, no window, no account. Launch at login, pick your language and units, and hide any row you do not care about.

install.title: Installing
install.body: Konechi is signed ad-hoc rather than notarised, so the first launch is met with an "unidentified developer" warning. Open System Settings, go to Privacy & Security, and allow it. After that it updates itself.
